items.title: Add a round timer and best-of-3 rounds
items.detail: A 60-second countdown in the HUD. When it hits zero, whoever has more health wins the round. First to two rounds wins the match. Between rounds, reset both fighters to their spawn points and refill health, with a short 'ROUND 2' banner. Show round pips next to each health bar. Add tests for the round-win and timeout-win conditions.
items.note: Built by hand (the API path was blocked). 60s clock, best of three, round pips, fighters reset between rounds. 9 tests in tools/rounds.test.mjs.

items.title: Add input buffering and a combo counter
items.detail: Buffer an attack press for ~150ms so a button hit slightly before the current move ends still registers, which is what makes chained attacks feel good. Track consecutive hits landed on a fighter within 1.2s of each other as a combo, and show the count in the HUD near that fighter's health bar. Reset on timeout or when the fighter recovers.
items.note: Add a configurable 150ms, single-slot buffer for punch/kick presses, consumed as soon as the state machine permits without cancelling moves. Track unblocked, damaging hits on each defender, clearing t

items.title: Make the camera track both fighters
items.detail: Instead of a fixed camera, keep both fighters framed: follow the midpoint on X/Z and pull back as they separate, clamped so it never leaves the arena or gets closer than the current framing. Smooth it with damping so it never snaps. Keep the same pitch and field of view.
items.note: Extend the existing camera update to follow the fighters’ midpoint on both X and Z, with arena-clamped tracking offsets and bounded pull-back along the camera’s viewing axis. Damp tracking and pull-ba

items.title: Add a main menu and pause screen
items.detail: A title screen before the fight with 'Fight the CPU', 'Two players' and a difficulty selector (which sets the AI's base aggression and think interval). Escape pauses mid-fight with resume and quit-to-menu. The game loop should stop advancing while paused. Keep it all in the existing DOM overlay style rather than rendering menus in three.js.
items.note: Add a DOM-based title/pause menu and a simulation gate that freezes every gameplay update while paused, without stopping rendering. Add configurable difficulty presets and per-controller AI settings;  [correction] menu.js was written but never imported by main.js, so the feature was not in the game. Wired in by hand on 2026-09-11, along with input.clearInput() and a match lifecycle. tools/wiring.test.mjs now fails on any orphaned module.

items.title: Add a second local player option
items.detail: Let the second fighter be driven by keyboardController('p2') instead of the AI, chosen from the menu. The p2 bindings already exist in input.js. Make sure the AI is not constructed at all in two-player mode so no API calls are made.
items.note: Add a startup menu for CPU or local two-player matches. Local mode uses `keyboardController('p2')` and never constructs the AI or calls the model bridge, including status and usage polling. CPU behavi

items.title: Add light and heavy attack variants
items.detail: Split the punch into a light jab (faster, less damage, less recovery) and a heavy punch (slower, more damage, more knockback) on separate buttons. Reuse the existing punch clip for both with different playback speeds until dedicated clips exist. Extend the AI's attack vocabulary to include them.
items.note: Add light and heavy punches on separate buttons, with configurable damage, knockback, and playback speeds that also scale startup and recovery. Both reuse `punch`; buffering, airborne punches, and per

items.title: Add hit-stop and a KO slow-motion finish
items.detail: Freeze both fighters for ~60ms when a heavy hit lands, which is what gives impacts weight. On the killing blow, drop the global time scale to about 0.35 for a second and push the camera slightly closer before the KO banner. Implement as a time-scale multiplier applied in the game loop so nothing else needs to know about it.
items.note: Add a loop-owned time multiplier: confirmed, unblocked heavy punches freeze simulation for 60 ms; lethal hits then play one second at 0.35× speed before round resolution and the KO banner. Add a small

items.title: Add procedural sound effects
items.detail: Use the Web Audio API to synthesise the sounds rather than shipping audio files: a short noise burst with a low thump for a landed hit, a duller filtered version for a blocked one, a whoosh for a whiffed swing, a thud on landing from a jump. Keep it in a new renderer/src/audio.js with a single play(name) entry point, and a master mute toggle on M.

items.title: Give each fighter its own stats
items.detail: Fighter reads speed, health and damage from module constants in config.js, so every fighter is identical and no roster is possible. Add an optional `stats` option to the Fighter constructor — maxHealth, walkSpeed, runSpeed, jumpSpeed, damageScale, defenceScale — stored on the instance and read everywhere the constants are read now. Omitting it must reproduce today's numbers exactly, so existing tests keep passing unchanged. damageScale multiplies damage this fighter deals; defenceScale divides damage it receives. Add tests proving: a fighter with damageScale 2 deals double, one with defenceScale 2 takes half, a faster walkSpeed covers more ground in the same dt, and a fighter built with no stats matches the config constants field for field.
items.note: The stats implementation and its tests are already present. The reported failures come from macOS AppleDouble metadata files (`._*.js`) being treated as JavaScript modules. Add a pretest cleanup that

items.title: Add a character roster
items.detail: New module renderer/src/characters.js. Export CHARACTERS: at least six fighters, each { id, name, tagline, tint, scale, stats, special }, where stats matches the shape item 9 added and special is a string id for now. Make the archetypes genuinely different — balanced, heavy and slow with high damage, fast and fragile, long-reach, defensive wall, glass cannon — by varying the stats, not just the names. Export characterById(id) falling back to the first character, and applyCharacter(model, character) which clones every material it touches before tinting, so two fighters never share a material instance, and applies scale. Pure data plus small functions: no DOM, and no scene access beyond the model passed in. Import it from main.js and use it when building fighters. Tests: ids unique, six or more, stats inside sane bounds, applyCharacter leaves the source material untouched, and two different characters cloned from one model end up with different material colours.
items.note: Add six stat-distinct fighters, with roster tuning in config.js and material-safe appearance helpers in characters.js. Match creation will apply roster names, stats, tint, and scale; defaults are Axel

items.title: Add four playable arenas
items.detail: New module renderer/src/arenas.js. Four maps built procedurally in three.js with no new art files: a dojo (warm wood floor, paper screens, hanging lanterns), a neon street at night (wet asphalt, coloured signage glow, rain-slick reflections), a temple courtyard (stone flags, pillars, dusk sky), and a rooftop (concrete, distant city lights, high fog). Export MAPS as { id, name, floorColor, skyColor, fog, lights, build(scene) } and buildMap(scene, mapId) returning a dispose() that removes every object and light it added and frees their geometries and materials. createArena(canvas, mapId) selects one. Switching map between matches must leave the scene's child count back where it started. Tests: ids unique, unknown id falls back to the first map, and build-then-dispose restores the exact scene child count and disposes what it created.
items.note: Add four procedural arenas with map-owned lighting, shared geometry, and idempotent cleanup. Keep combat bounds, fighters, and camera behavior unchanged. Add an arena selector between matches, safe ma

items.title: Add a pre-fight selection state machine
items.detail: New module renderer/src/select-state.js, pure and DOM-free so it can be tested in node. Export createSelectState({ characters, maps, twoPlayer }) modelling the flow mode -> P1 character -> P2 character -> map -> ready. In one-player mode the CPU picks its own character, so that step is skipped and filled in automatically. Methods: move(delta) to move the cursor, choose() to confirm the highlighted entry, back() to return to the previous step (and from the first step, to report that the caller should leave the flow), plus getters step, cursor, options, selection and canStart. back() must clear the choice it is undoing. Test it exhaustively: every path through the flow, back() from each step, cursor wrapping at both ends, and that selection is only complete when canStart is true.
items.note: Landed as renderer/src/match-selection.js under item 13, with tools/match-selection.test.mjs. Closed 2026-09-11.

items.title: Show character and map select in the menu
items.detail: Render the item-12 state machine in menu.js, between choosing a mode and starting the match: a grid of character cards showing name, tagline and a tint swatch, then a map grid, with the highlighted entry visibly selected. Drive it with arrow keys and Enter as well as the mouse, keep the existing focus trap and Escape behaviour, and add a Back control. onStart must now receive { mode, difficulty, ai, p1Character, p2Character, map } and main.js must use all of them — build each fighter through applyCharacter with its own stats, and create the arena with the chosen map. Do not put game logic in menu.js; it renders the state machine and nothing more. Every new module must be imported from main.js or something main.js imports, or tools/wiring.test.mjs will fail.
items.note: Add a small, headless selection state machine for mode → P1 character → P2/CPU character → map. The menu will render its cards, selection highlight, keyboard navigation and Back control while preservi

items.title: Add a super meter and per-character specials
items.detail: A meter per fighter that fills as it deals and takes damage, capped, and spends in full when a special is thrown. Put the meter maths in its own pure module so it is testable. Give each roster character a distinct special keyed off character.special: a forward projectile, a rising uppercut, a spinning multi-hit kick, a ground pound with a shockwave, a dashing shoulder charge, and a short counter stance that punishes the next hit. Reuse the existing animation clips rather than inventing new ones — a special is a state with its own timing, damage, reach and cancel rules. Show the meter in the HUD under each health bar. Bind it to a new key per player. Tests: the meter fills and clamps, a special cannot fire below full, firing empties it, and each special's damage and reach differ.
items.note: Superseded by item 24, which specifies the meter and the supers properly instead of leaving "special" as a bare string id. Original attempt failed on an Azure server error, not on the work.

items.title: Add grabs and throws
items.detail: A grab that only connects at close range against a fighter who is not already being thrown, is not invulnerable, and is not mid-special. On connection the victim enters a held state for a short window during which a direction plus attack throws them forward or backward, and no input escapes it except a mash that breaks out if pressed fast enough. A throw deals damage, sets knockdown, and cannot be comboed into another grab immediately. Blocking does not stop a grab — that is the point of grabs — but a grab is slower to start than a jab. Bind it to a new key per player. Tests: range gating, break-out on a fast mash, no break-out on a slow one, throw damage and direction, and that a grab cannot chain into a second grab within the cooldown.
items.note: Normalize signed zero in both throw launch velocity components. A backward depth-axis throw currently multiplies zero by a negative direction, producing `-0`; adding positive zero after scaling preser

items.title: Add air attacks and juggles
items.detail: Attacks while airborne: a jumping light, a jumping heavy and a diving kick that commits the fighter downward. A fighter hit while airborne enters a juggle state, staying in hitstun and floating briefly so a follow-up can connect, with a per-combo juggle limit so it cannot loop forever and diminishing damage as the juggle count rises. Landing cancels the air state. Tests: an air attack only starts off the floor, juggle count increments per airborne hit, damage scales down as it rises, the limit ends the juggle, and landing resets it.

items.title: Widen the key bindings and generate the on-screen controls
items.detail: INPUT_MAPS needs entries for the new actions — special, grab, taunt — for both players, chosen so they are comfortable on one keyboard and never collide with each other or with the mute key. Then stop hand-writing the control hints: the text in index.html is already stale, still promising 'J punch' when J is a light jab and I is a heavy. Generate the on-screen hints from INPUT_MAPS at runtime, with a readable label per physical key code, so the two can never drift apart again. Add a test asserting no key code is bound twice within a player's map, that the two players' maps do not overlap, that neither claims the mute key, and that every action in the map has a label.

items.title: Bring the camera down to the fight
items.detail: The camera sits at y 10, z 9.5, pitched -38 degrees with a 40 degree field of view, which leaves the fighters small in the middle of a mostly empty frame and the top third of the screen showing nothing. Lower it and bring it in so the fighters fill the frame the way they do in a beat-'em-up, keeping the existing follow, separation pull-back and KO push-in behaviour intact. Let each map override the camera so the rooftop can sit lower than the temple. Add a test that the resolved camera for every map keeps both fighters inside the view frustum at maximum separation and at the arena's corners.

items.title: Load a separate model per character, falling back to the knight
items.detail: Right now every character is the same knight with a different tint. Let a character optionally name its own .glb under renderer/assets/characters/, load it once and cache it, and clone per fighter exactly as the knight is cloned. A character with no model, or whose model fails to load, must silently fall back to the tinted knight — a missing file is never fatal, the same rule the clip loader already follows. Animation clips stay shared, so a model whose skeleton does not match the mixamorig bone names should be rejected at load time and fall back rather than animate wrongly. Tests: fallback on a missing model, fallback on a skeleton mismatch, and that the cache loads a shared model only once.

items.title: Rebuild the stages at Little Fighter 2 scale
items.detail:
The playable area is 4.8 by 4.8 units — a small square the fighters bounce off. Little Fighter 2 stages are WIDE: you walk for a long time left and right, and only a little toward and away from the camera. Rebuild for that shape.

Split MAP_ART.floorSize into floorWidth and floorDepth and update all eleven uses in arenas.js, choosing per-axis correctly: the rooftop's back parapet and any prop that runs left-to-right spans floorWidth; the side parapets, street curbs and anything running toward the camera span floorDepth. Set floorWidth to about 48 and floorDepth to about 14, and set ARENA.limitX and limitZ from those minus a margin, so a fighter can walk roughly ten body-lengths end to end and about two across. Move the spawns further apart to suit.

Then make the art actually fill that width instead of huddling in the middle. Every prop currently placed at a hand-written x — the dojo's five paper screens and three lanterns, the street's signage and curbs, the temple's pillars, the rooftop's towers — must repeat across the full width at a sensible spacing rather than being stretched or left clustered at the centre. Vary them with the existing noise() so the repetition does not read as wallpaper.

Watch the cost: addTiles builds one mesh per tile, so a wider floor multiplies the count. Use THREE.InstancedMesh for the tiles, planks and any prop repeated more than about twenty times, so a bigger stage does not cost frame rate. Keep every map's dispose() releasing what it created — instanced or not.

The camera must follow across the width: CAMERA.maxOffsetX has to grow with the stage, while maxOffsetZ stays small. Keep the fighters framed at the ends of the stage, not just at the centre.

Tests: floorWidth is at least three times floorDepth; ARENA.limitX is at least eight times BODY.radius; every map's dispose() returns the scene to its starting child count; the total mesh count per map stays under a stated budget; and the camera keeps both fighters inside the frustum with one at each end of the stage.

items.title: Give every character a real move list, not a stat block
items.detail:
characters.js is 1.4 KB: six entries differing only by tint, scale and six numbers. The fighters are the same knight in different colours with the same eight buttons. That is the single biggest gap in the game.

Add renderer/src/moves.js: a data-driven move table plus the pure logic that resolves an input into a move. A move is { id, name, input, startup, active, recovery, damage, knockback, knocksDown, reach, hitHeight ('low' | 'mid' | 'high' | 'air'), cancelInto, meterGain, vfx, sound, clip, clipSpeed }. `input` is a command, not a single button: a direction sequence plus a button, in the Street Fighter idiom — 'forward,down,light', 'back,back,heavy', 'down,up,kick' — resolved against a short input history so a player can actually perform it. `cancelInto` lists the move ids this move may be cancelled into during its recovery, which is what turns single hits into strings.

Give EACH of the six characters eight to twelve moves, and make them play differently, not just hit for different numbers:
  Axel (balanced) — a three-hit jab string, a launcher, a sweep, a rushing elbow, an anti-air uppercut, a command grab.
  Rook (heavy) — slow armoured swings that shrug off one hit during startup, a ground pound with a shockwave that hits both sides, a running shoulder, a lariat.
  Zip (fast) — four-hit strings, a teleport dash, a run-cancel, an air dive, hit-and-run moves with tiny damage and huge speed.
  Pike (reach) — long pokes that control space, a thrust with a long active window, a counter-poke that beats approaches, a low slide.
  Bastion (defensive) — a parry that converts into a punish, a guard-cancel push, a reversal that only works from block, high defence and low mobility.
  Ember (glass cannon) — enormous damage, almost no defence, a projectile, a diving flame kick, a self-damaging overdrive.

Keep moves.js pure: no THREE, no DOM, no timers. Export the tables plus resolveMove(history, character, state) and canCancel(from, into). fighter.js consults it rather than reimplementing it, and keeps its existing states working — moves are an addition, not a replacement.

Tests, thoroughly: every move id is unique per character; every cancelInto target exists; startup, active and recovery are all positive and sum to a sane duration; a command is recognised from a correct input history and rejected from a wrong one, including a near-miss with one direction wrong; commands time out if entered too slowly; longer commands win over shorter ones that are a prefix of them; each character's total damage output over its best string differs meaningfully from the others'; and no move both knocks down and cancels into another move, which would be an infinite.
items.note: tests failed: # pass 192 # fail 12

items.title: Add a visual effects system with real impact
items.detail:
Hits currently spawn one small coloured sphere. Modern fighting games sell a hit with layered effects, and the game has none of that.

Add renderer/src/vfx.js: a pooled effect system built procedurally in three.js, with no external assets and no new dependencies. Effects to implement, each parameterised by position, direction, scale and colour:
  * impact flash — a bright expanding billboard that fades in under 0.15s
  * spark burst — a dozen short streaks thrown outward along the hit direction
  * shockwave — an expanding ground ring, for ground pounds and heavy landings
  * lightning — a jagged branching polyline between two points, regenerated a few times a second so it crackles, with an additive glow
  * energy projectile — a glowing core with a trailing tail that can travel and expire
  * afterimage — a few fading copies of the fighter's pose during a dash or teleport
  * dust — puffs at the feet on landing, dashing and being knocked down
  * screen shake — a short camera offset that decays, scaled by the hit's weight
  * hit spark colour by move weight, so a light jab and a super do not look alike

Pool and reuse geometry and materials; never allocate per frame in the update loop. One update(dt) drives everything, and one clear() empties it between rounds. Wire it so every move's `vfx` id from item 21 selects an effect, the arena owns the instance, and screen shake reaches the camera without fighting the existing tracking, pull-back and KO push-in.

Tests, headless: effects expire and are returned to the pool; the pool never grows beyond its cap under sustained spawning; clear() releases everything and disposes what it allocated; screen shake decays to exactly zero and never leaves the camera offset; an unknown vfx id is ignored rather than throwing; and the lightning generator produces a connected path between its two endpoints every time.
items.note: tests failed: # pass 193 # fail 11

items.title: Give every move its own sound
items.detail:
audio.js synthesises four sounds: hit, block, whiff, land. Every attack in the game sounds the same, which flattens all of item 21's variety back out.

Extend the procedural synthesis — still no audio files — so each move's `sound` id from item 21 maps to its own voice, and build the vocabulary the move list needs: a light jab's short bright snap, a heavy's low thud with body, a whoosh that pitches with the swing's speed, a metallic clash when two attacks trade, a parry's chime, a grab's cloth-and-impact, a throw's landing crack, an electric crackle for lightning moves, a projectile's launch and its impact, a deep boom for a ground pound, a rising sweep for a super's activation, and a KO stinger.

Layer them the way the existing sounds already do — a filtered noise burst plus a pitched tone — and vary pitch slightly per trigger so repeated jabs do not sound like a loop. Respect the existing voice cap, mute key and master volume, and keep dropping sounds rather than queueing them when the cap is hit.

Tests: every sound id referenced by a move exists in the table; every envelope has a positive duration and a non-zero volume; the voice cap is never exceeded under a burst of triggers; muting silences new sounds; and pitch variation stays inside a stated range so nothing ever sounds wrong rather than merely different.

items.title: Add a super meter and one signature super per character
items.detail:
Put the meter maths in its own pure module, renderer/src/meter.js, so it is testable without a fighter: it fills from damage dealt and damage taken at different rates, caps at a full bar, has stocks rather than a single bar so a player can bank one, and spends a whole stock on activation. Carry it between rounds or reset it, but decide deliberately and say which in a comment.

Then give each character from item 21 one signature super that costs a stock, using the vfx and sound vocabulary from items 22 and 23:
  Axel — a rushing multi-hit combination ending in a launcher
  Rook — a leaping ground pound with a screen-wide shockwave
  Zip — a teleport flurry that strikes from several positions in sequence
  Pike — a long committed thrust that pierces a block
  Bastion — a counter stance that, if struck during it, answers with a full punish
  Ember — a lightning column that sets the point of impact alight

A super gets brief invulnerability during its startup, a short cinematic pause on connection, and cannot be cancelled into another move. Show the meter and its stocks in the HUD under each health bar, filling smoothly rather than jumping.

Tests: the meter fills, caps and banks stocks correctly; activation below a full stock is refused and consumes nothing; activation spends exactly one stock; damage dealt and damage taken fill at their stated different rates; a super cannot be cancelled into; its startup invulnerability begins and ends on the stated frames; and each character's super differs in damage, reach and duration.
items.note: tests failed: # pass 189 # fail 18

items.title: Teach the CPU to use the move list
items.detail:
ai.js presses the old eight buttons. After items 21 and 24 it would fight with a fraction of its character's kit while the human has all of it, which reads as the CPU being stupid rather than as a difficulty setting.

Let the AI pick moves from its own character's table: perform the command inputs through the same resolution path a player uses rather than bypassing it, choose by range band (close, mid, far) and situation (opponent airborne, blocking, recovering, knocked down), continue a string by cancelling where the table allows it, hold a super for a punish rather than throwing it on cooldown, and respect the existing difficulty presets — an Easy CPU should use short strings and miss punishes, a Hard one should convert them.

Keep the model bridge exactly as it is: the Azure plan re-weights preferences, and the local layer stays in the critical path so no key and no reply still plays fine.

Tests: the AI only ever selects moves its own character owns; commands it emits are accepted by the same resolver a player's input goes through; it prefers a longer-reach move at longer range; it does not attempt a knocked-down opponent; and Easy produces measurably shorter strings than Hard over a simulated exchange.
